newsitem.title: CHINA: China sentences two democracy activists to labour.
newsitem.headline: China sentences two democracy activists to labour.

text.p: China has sentenced two democracy activists to a labour camp for up to three years, accusing them of writing subversive materials, a fellow dissident said on Saturday.

Authorities in the city of Taiyuan in central China's Shanxi province had sentenced Fu Guoyong to three years of re-education through labour and fellow activist Chen Ping to one year, the dissident told Reuters by telephone.
"The reason was because they published articles abroad about democracy," said the dissident, who asked not to be identified.
Taiyuan police had detained Fu in July and had notified his family of the sentencing on November 19, he said.
Family members were not immediately available for comment.
Fu moved to Taiyuan in late June, complaining of repeated harassment by police in Hangzhou city in the eastern province of Zhejiang, where he had been living with his wife.
Chen, who had worked with Fu on pro-democracy writings, had been detained in Taiyuan in August and was sentenced at the same time as Fu, he said.
"They just wrote some articles. There really was no reason for this," the dissident said in reference to the sentences.

Fu, 29, previously served two years in a labour camp for his role in the student-led demonstrations in Beijing's Tiananmen Square that were crushed by the military with heavy loss of life on June 4, 1989.

Police detained Fu for more than a month in December 1995 after he, along with other activists, wrote a letter calling for the release of Wei Jingsheng, one of the fathers of China's democracy movement.
The sentences came amid a widening crackdown on dissent by Beijing. Most dissidents are already serving time in prison or labour camps or have been forced into exile.
Beijing dismisses criticism of its human rights record as interference in its internal affairs.
Last week a Chinese court sentenced 56-year-old dissident Zhang Zong'ai to five years in prison for counter-revolutionary incitement.
Three pro-democracy activists are currently standing trial on charges of counter-revolutionary propaganda and incitement in Hefei, capital of the central province of Anhui.
In the southern boomtown of Shenzhen that neighbours Hong Kong, two labour activists are standing trial for conspiring to subvert the government.
